speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms: does the weakness affect all muscles in your right arm, or is it specific to certain areas? Also, have you noticed any changes in your sensation, such as tingling or numbness?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, heavy alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use, have you noticed any neck pain, fever, or recent neck trauma prior to the onset of arm weakness? Additionally, does the weakness involve your hand grip strength specifically?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Neuritis (Parsonage-Turner Syndrome) with secondary amyotrophy.

The diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis is unlikely given your age, lack of other neurological deficits, and the severe weight loss; your symptoms are more consistent with an inflammatory brachial neuritis complicated by steroid-induced muscle atrophy. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine, EMG/Nerve Conduction Study Right Upper Extremity.
